proofs.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{lem:blocked-model-geometry}\), \(I_p\) is a smooth point of every blocked model and
\[
 T_C^{\circ}=\operatorname{span}\{v_{jB}:j\in V,\ B\in\Pi_j\},
 \qquad \operatorname{supp}(v_{jB})=\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}.
\]
Every unordered skeleton edge occurs in exactly one such support: it is assigned to the partition block at its unique head, and blocks at a fixed head are disjoint. Hence distinct generators have disjoint supports.

If \(w=\sum_{j,B}a_{jB}v_{jB}\neq0\), disjointness gives
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(w)=\bigcup_{a_{jB}\neq0}\operatorname{supp}(v_{jB});
\]
there is no coordinate cancellation. It follows in both directions that the inclusion-minimal nonempty supports of vectors in \(T_C^{\circ}\) are precisely the individual generator supports. Their union is \(\operatorname{skel}(G)\).

Equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies equality of their tangent spaces at their common point \(I_p\), and therefore equality of these support partitions. A support containing at least two distinct edges is a star with a unique common endpoint. That endpoint must be the head \(j\), and the other endpoints recover the labelled block \(B\); these are exactly the members of \(\mathcal N_j(C)\). A one-edge support has no distinguishable endpoint and recovers only its underlying unordered edge. Applying the same argument to \(D\) proves skeleton equality and \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\). If an edge reverses, it cannot belong to any recovered nonsingleton block in either state, so it is a singleton block in both.

By \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\), the edge is singleton in both states and the labelled nonsingleton families agree targetwise between \(C\) and \(D\). By \(\texttt{lem:edge-coloured-model-equivalence-markov}\), \(G\) and \(H\) have the same unshielded colliders.

Fix \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) and \(s\in S\). Tangent recovery gives \(s\to x\) in both graphs. If \(s\) and \(y\) were nonadjacent, then \(s\to x\to y\) in \(G\) would become the unshielded collider \(s\to x\leftarrow y\) in \(H\), impossible. Thus \(s\) and \(y\) are adjacent. The orientation \(y\to s\) in \(G\) would create the directed cycle \(y\to s\to x\to y\), so \(s\to y\). Since \(s\) was arbitrary,
\[
 S\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_G(y).
\]

Suppose that \(S\) is not contained in one block of \(\Pi_y\). Then some \(T\in\Pi_y\) meets but does not contain \(S\). Because \(\{x\}\) is the singleton block containing the reversed edge, \(x\notin T\). In the model for \(C\), set every innovation variance to one, set the coefficients on \(x\to y\) and on the block \(T\) to one, and set all other block coefficients to zero. These are admitted parameter values under \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\). Every variable other than \(X_y\) is then an independent standard Gaussian, while
\[
 X_y=X_x+\sum_{r\in T}X_r+\varepsilon_y.
\]
The resulting covariance is positive definite because it is generated with strictly positive innovation variances.

Let \(P=\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\) and \(Q=P\setminus\{y\}\). The preceding graph argument and targetwise tangent recovery give \(S\subseteq Q\). Residualizing \(X_y\) against \(X_Q\) leaves
\[
 Z=X_x+\sum_{r\in T\setminus Q}X_r+\varepsilon_y,\qquad
 h=\operatorname{Var}(Z)=2+|T\setminus Q|>0.
\]
All displayed summands are mutually independent. Therefore the coefficient on \(X_y\) in the regression of \(X_x\) on \((X_Q,X_y)\) is
\[
 q=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(X_x,Z)}{\operatorname{Var}(Z)}
 =\frac1{2+|T\setminus Q|}>0.
\]
Before adding \(X_y\), the regression coefficient on every \(X_s\), \(s\in Q\), is zero. The residualization identity therefore gives the final coefficient
\[
 -q\,\mathbf 1\{s\in T\},\qquad s\in S.
\]
Since \(T\cap S\neq\varnothing\) and \(S\nsubseteq T\), these coefficients take both values \(-q\) and \(0\) on \(S\). But \(S\in\mathcal N_x(D)\), so every covariance in \(\mathcal M(D)\) must have equal parent-regression coefficients on \(S\), by the recovery formula in \(\texttt{lem:blocked-model-geometry}\). The constructed covariance lies in \(\mathcal M(C)\setminus\mathcal M(D)\), contradicting model equality. Hence each \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) is contained in a member \(T\in\mathcal N_y(C)\).

Apply the same argument after exchanging \(C,D\) and \(x,y\). Every such \(T\) is contained in a member \(U\in\mathcal N_x(C)\). Thus \(S\subseteq T\subseteq U\). Since \(S\) and \(U\) are intersecting blocks in the same partition at \(x\), they are equal; hence \(S=T=U\). This proves \(\mathcal N_x(C)\subseteq\mathcal N_y(C)\), and symmetry gives the reverse inclusion.

We prove the three implications.

Suppose first that \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\). The lemma \(\texttt{lem:edge-coloured-model-equivalence-markov}\) gives equality of skeletons and unshielded colliders. The lemma \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\) gives
\(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\). If an edge has opposite orientations, \(\texttt{lem:reversed-edge-separator}\) says that its endpoint families are equal. Equivalently, every edge whose endpoint families are unequal has the same orientation in the two graphs. With the common skeleton and common family map, this is precisely \(F(C)=F(D)\). Hence \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\).

Conversely suppose \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\). By \(\texttt{lem:verma-pearl-markov-equivalence}\), the common skeleton and unshielded colliders make \(G\) and \(H\) Markov equivalent. Apply \(\texttt{lem:chickering-monotone-covered-reversals}\): there are \(\delta(C,D)\) distinct covered reversals taking \(G\) to \(H\), every one on an edge whose initial orientation disagrees with \(H\). We lift this graph sequence to blocked states inductively.

The nonsingleton families at the start are the common families \(\mathcal N_j=\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\). Consider a covered edge \(i\to j\) selected at an intermediate graph. It is one of the initially disagreeing edges. If \(\mathcal N_i\neq\mathcal N_j\), equality of \(F(C)\) and \(F(D)\) would force its orientation to agree in \(G\) and \(H\), a contradiction. Thus \(\mathcal N_i=\mathcal N_j\).

The edge \(i\to j\) is a singleton block at the current target \(j\). Indeed, if it belonged to \(B\in\mathcal N_j\), equality of endpoint families would give \(B\in\mathcal N_i\); but \(i\in B\) is impossible because no vertex is its own parent. Coveredness gives
\[
 \operatorname{pa}(j)=\operatorname{pa}(i)\cup\{i\}.
\]
On the common parent set, the two partitions have the identical nonsingleton blocks \(\mathcal N_i=\mathcal N_j\). Every parent not covered by one of those blocks must be a singleton in both partitions. Therefore
\[
 \Pi_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi_i,
\]
so this covered reversal is exactly the defined move in \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\). By \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\), it preserves every nonsingleton family, validating the induction. After all \(\delta(C,D)\) steps the graph is \(H\). At every vertex, its parent set together with the fixed nonsingleton family uniquely determines its partition: append singleton blocks for precisely the parents outside the union of the nonsingleton blocks. Hence the final partition is \(\Lambda\), and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\).

If \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\), repeated application of \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\) gives \(\mathcal M(D)=\mathcal M(C)\). This completes equivalence of the three conditions.

The lifted Chickering path has length \(\delta(C,D)\) and reverses each disagreeing edge once. Conversely, any legal-reversal path changes the orientation of only one skeleton edge per step. Each of the \(\delta(C,D)\) edges on which the endpoints disagree must be reversed an odd number of times, so every path has length at least \(\delta(C,D)\). Thus
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D).
\]

Finally suppose every block of \(C\) is nonsingleton. For every edge \(i\to j\), its block \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) contains \(i\), whereas no member of \(\mathcal N_i(C)\) can contain \(i\). Hence \(\mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)\), so the static criterion fixes every arrow. The parent sets, together with the nonsingleton families, then fix every partition, and \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\). This recovers the cited BPEC identifiability boundary \(\texttt{lem:bpec-proper-identifiability}\); allowing singleton blocks strictly enlarges the class, while the theorem still characterizes it.

The visited set in \(\texttt{def:component-enumerator}\) is, by construction, the smallest subset of \(\mathfrak S_p\) containing \(C\) and closed under every defined legal reversal. Since every move is invertible by \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\), this set is exactly \(\mathcal R(C)\). The main theorem then gives
\[
 \operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)
 =\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}.
\]

The state space is finite: there are finitely many directed graphs on \(V\), and every finite parent set has finitely many partitions. Exact memoization therefore makes breadth-first search terminate and prevents duplicate state emission.

For the sharper bound, assign to each emitted DAG its lexicographically first topological ordering. A fixed skeleton and a topological ordering determine every arrow, because each edge must point from the earlier endpoint to the later endpoint. Thus this assignment is injective on the DAGs in the component. For a fixed graph in the component, the main theorem fixes every \(\mathcal N_j\), and the parent set and \(\mathcal N_j\) uniquely determine the partition by making every remaining parent a singleton. Hence there is at most one component state per DAG and
\[
 |\operatorname{Enum}(C)|=|\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!.
\]

Using a \(p\)-by-\(p\) adjacency matrix, skeleton comparison costs \(O(p^2)\). Enumerating triples and checking whether two incoming adjacent edges form an unshielded collider costs \(O(p^3)\). At each vertex, place a block bitset in the array position indexed by its least member; because blocks are disjoint, this canonicalization and comparison examines at most \(p^2\) bit positions per vertex. Comparing the already oriented family-mismatch edge sets costs \(O(p^2)\). Thus all family and orientation comparisons cost \(O(p^3)\), and static equality has the asserted bound.

Breadth-first search in an unweighted graph records a predecessor when a state is first discovered, so its predecessor path has minimum legal-reversal length. By the main theorem that length is \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\) for every emitted \(D\).

If every block of \(C\) is a singleton, then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for every \(j\), so \(F(C)=\varnothing\). The static criterion of \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) then reduces exactly to equality of skeleton and unshielded colliders. By \(\texttt{lem:verma-pearl-markov-equivalence}\), this is the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\), and the distance equality in the theorem gives \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}=\delta\).

If no block of \(C\) is a singleton, take any edge \(i\to j\). Its block \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) contains \(i\), while no block at \(i\) can contain \(i\). Hence \(\mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)\). Every edge therefore belongs to \(F(C)\) and its orientation is fixed by the static criterion. Once the graph is fixed, the fixed nonsingleton families give the whole partition because there is no singleton remainder. Thus \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), agreeing with the cited BPEC boundary.

Finally, if \(G=H\) and the models are equal, \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\) gives \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) at every vertex. Their parent sets are already identical. A partition is uniquely the displayed nonsingleton blocks together with singleton blocks for all remaining parents, so \(\Pi_j=\Lambda_j\) for every \(j\), and \(\Pi=\Lambda\).

Write \(d_E=p+\sum_j|\Pi^E_j|\). By \(\texttt{lem:blocked-model-geometry}\), \(\mathcal M(E)\) is a connected, relatively closed embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\) of dimension \(d_E\), described there by finitely many polynomial equalities after positive denominators are cleared.

We first justify properness of \(\mathcal E_C\). Fix \(D\) with \(d_D\leq d_C\) and \(\mathcal M(D)\neq\mathcal M(C)\). If \(d_D<d_C\), an embedded \(d_C\)-manifold cannot be contained in an embedded \(d_D\)-manifold. If \(d_D=d_C\) and \(\mathcal M(C)\subseteq\mathcal M(D)\), equal-dimensional manifold charts make the inclusion locally open, while relative closedness makes \(\mathcal M(C)\) closed in \(\mathcal M(D)\). Connectedness of \(\mathcal M(D)\) would then imply equality, a contradiction. Thus \(\mathcal M(C)\nsubseteq\mathcal M(D)\). At least one polynomial equality defining \(\mathcal M(D)\) consequently pulls back under \(\phi_C\) to a nonzero polynomial on \(\Theta_C\). Its zero set contains the relevant intersection pullback used in \(\texttt{def:generic-exception}\).

For a reported effect coordinate that is nonconstant on \(\mathcal M(C)\), its rational composition with \(\phi_C\) is nonconstant; hence its derivative is not identically zero. Clearing its positive Gram denominators shows that its zero-gradient locus is also contained in the zero set of a nonzero polynomial. There are only finitely many states and reported coordinates. The product of the resulting nonzero polynomials is nonzero, so its zero set cannot contain the open parameter domain \(\Theta_C\). Therefore \(\mathcal E_C\subsetneq\Theta_C\) is proper algebraic. Since \(\theta_C\notin\mathcal E_C\),
\[
 \Sigma_0\notin\mathcal M(D)
 \quad\text{for every nonequivalent }D\text{ with }d_D\leq d_C.
\]

By \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\), \(S_n\) is positive definite almost surely for every \(n\geq p\). For nonempty \(P_{Ej}\), the block-incidence matrix has full column rank because its nonempty block columns have disjoint supports. Hence
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)u
 =(A_{Ej}u)^{\mathsf T}S_{n,P_{Ej}P_{Ej}}(A_{Ej}u)>0
\]
for every \(u\neq0\). The residual variance is the Schur complement after regression on the full-rank block-sum design and is strictly positive. Thus the likelihood branch in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\) is finite and attained.

For completeness, compare the criteria directly. Up to a constant independent of \(\Sigma\),
\[
 \ell_n(\Sigma)=-\frac n2\{\log\det\Sigma+operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^{-1}S_n)\}.
\]
The population likelihood contrast is
\[
 K(\Sigma_0,\Sigma)=\frac12\left\{
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^{-1}\Sigma_0)
 -\log\det(\Sigma^{-1}\Sigma_0)-p\right\}\geq0.
\]
Diagonalizing \(\Sigma^{-1/2}\Sigma_0\Sigma^{-1/2}\) reduces the inequality to \(u-\log u-1\geq0\), with equality only at \(u=1\); hence equality holds only for \(\Sigma=\Sigma_0\). Its sublevel sets are compact inside the positive-definite cone because the same scalar expression diverges when an eigenvalue tends to zero or infinity. Relative closedness of \(\mathcal M(D)\) and \(\Sigma_0\notin\mathcal M(D)\) therefore give
\[
 \kappa_D:=\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(D)}K(\Sigma_0,\Sigma)>0
\]
for every nonequivalent \(D\) with \(d_D\leq d_C\). Since \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\) in probability, the sample contrast converges uniformly on each such compact sublevel set; outside one fixed sublevel set it is uniformly worse with probability tending one. Consequently
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(D)}\ell_n(\Sigma)
 -\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(C)}\ell_n(\Sigma)
 \leq-n\kappa_D+o_{\mathbb P}(n).
\]
The \(O(\log n)\) penalty difference cannot offset this loss.

If instead \(d_D>d_C\), let \(\ell_n(S_n)\) denote the saturated maximum. Because \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M(C)\),
\[
 \sup_{\mathcal M(D)}\ell_n-\sup_{\mathcal M(C)}\ell_n
 \leq \ell_n(S_n)-\ell_n(\Sigma_0).
\]
Writing \(S_n=\Sigma_0+\Delta_n\), the first-order terms in the Taylor expansion of the right-hand side cancel, and \(\sqrt n\Delta_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\) by \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\). Hence
\[
 \ell_n(S_n)-\ell_n(\Sigma_0)=O_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \operatorname{BIC}_n(D)-\operatorname{BIC}_n(C)
 \geq(d_D-d_C)\log n-O_{\mathbb P}(1)\longrightarrow+\infty
\]
in probability.

The class \(\mathfrak S_p\) is finite, so with probability tending one every nonequivalent state loses to \(C\). Every remaining minimizer has covariance model \(\mathcal M(C)\); such states have dimension \(d_C\) because equal embedded images have equal dimension. The main equivalence theorem then yields \(\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\). The argument concerns the stated global minimizer only and makes no assertion about greedy search.

First connect the observable functionals to the causal target. If \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), the main theorem gives \(\mathcal M(E)=\mathcal M(C)\), so \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M(E)\). In the acyclic structural model for \(E\), the innovation at target \(j\) is independent of its parents. Therefore its population parent-regression coefficient is its structural coefficient row. The block-constrained normal equations in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\) have a unique solution, so
\[
 L_E(\Sigma_0)=B_E.
\]
Under an intervention on coordinate \(a\), differentiating the acyclic structural equations with respect to the intervention level gives the path-sum vector \((I_p-B_E)^{-1}e_a\). Hence \(((I_p-B_E)^{-1})_{ya}\) is the total causal effect of \(a\) on \(y\). It follows that \(g_E(\Sigma_0)\) is the member-labelled causal-effect vector, and \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\) is the finite causal target rather than its estimator.

By \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\), \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) almost surely for \(n\geq p\) and \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\) in probability. Positive definiteness and the full column rank of each block-incidence matrix make every \(\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)\) positive definite, so the maps and derivatives in the statement are evaluated on their declared open domain.

Let \(A_n=\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\}\). The BIC theorem gives \(\Pr(A_n)\to1\). On \(A_n\), the two components have the same finite index set and continuity of every rational \(g_E\) at \(\Sigma_0\) yields
\[
 d_H\{\mathcal T_{\widehat C_n}(S_n),\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\}
 \leq\max_{E\in\mathcal R(C)}\|g_E(S_n)-g_E(\Sigma_0)\|\ \xrightarrow{\mathbb P}\ 0.
\]
Outside \(A_n\) the probability tends to zero, proving unconditional Hausdorff convergence in probability.

For simultaneous coverage, retain member labels even when numerical effect values coincide. Flatten the finitely many member and query coordinates. Coordinates that are identically zero are covered by their singleton intervals with probability one. For every remaining coordinate \(f=g_{E,k}\), the exclusion \(\theta_C\notin\mathcal E_C\) gives \(\mathrm Df(\Sigma_0)\neq0\). The covariance of Gaussian sample-covariance coordinates is
\[
 (V_0)_{ij,kl}=\Sigma_{0,ik}\Sigma_{0,jl}+\Sigma_{0,il}\Sigma_{0,jk}.
\]
It is positive definite on nonzero symmetric derivatives by \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\). Thus each plug-in studentized error converges marginally to \(N(0,1)\). If \(K\geq1\) is the fixed number of these labelled nonconstant coordinates, each two-sided interval with critical value \(z_{1-\alpha/(2K)}\) has limiting noncoverage at most \(\alpha/K\). The union bound, which requires no nonsingularity of the stacked covariance, gives
\[
 \limsup_n\Pr\{\text{some labelled coordinate is not covered}\}\leq\alpha.
\]
When \(K=0\), all intervals are exact and the same assertion is immediate. Finally,
\[
 \Pr(A_n\cap\{\text{all labelled coordinates covered}\})
 \geq 1-\Pr(A_n^c)-\Pr\{\text{some coordinate is not covered}\},
\]
and taking the lower limit proves the displayed bound. Coincident member values do not change the labelled union bound, and a singular joint covariance is harmless because only the positive marginal variances are studentized.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), the map \(\phi_E:\Theta_E\to\mathbb S^p_{++}\) is an injective smooth embedding with connected, relatively closed image \(\mathcal M(E)\) of dimension \(p+\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^E_j|\). At the identity, its differential satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{proj}_{\mathrm{off}}T_{I_p}\mathcal M(E)
 =\operatorname{span}\{v_{jB}:j\in V,\ B\in\Pi^E_j\},
 \qquad (v_{jB})_{\{i,j\}}=\mathbf 1\{i\in B\}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal M(E)\) is the common zero set, inside \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), of finitely many rational equalities whose denominators are positive principal minors; after clearing those denominators the equalities are polynomial.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(E\). Acyclicity in \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\) gives a topological order. Hence \(B_E\) is nilpotent in that order and
\[
 (I_p-B_E)^{-1}=I_p+B_E+\cdots+B_E^{p-1}.
\]
Thus \(\phi_E\) is polynomial in \((\beta_E,\omega_E)\) and takes values in \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), because \(\operatorname{diag}(\omega_E)\) is positive definite by \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\).

Let \(P_j=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)\). In the structural equation
\[
 X_j=(B_E)_{jP_j}X_{P_j}+\varepsilon_j,
\]
every coordinate of \(X_{P_j}\) is a function only of innovations preceding \(j\) in a topological order. It is therefore independent of \(\varepsilon_j\). Consequently, for \(\Sigma=\phi_E(\beta_E,\omega_E)\),
\[
 (B_E)_{jP_j}=\Sigma_{jP_j}\Sigma_{P_jP_j}^{-1},
 \qquad
 \omega_{Ej}=\Sigma_{jj}-\Sigma_{jP_j}\Sigma_{P_jP_j}^{-1}\Sigma_{P_jj}.
\]
Every principal matrix \(\Sigma_{P_jP_j}\) is positive definite, including the empty case by the usual empty-matrix convention. These formulas give a rational smooth left inverse of \(\phi_E\) on its image. Thus \(\phi_E\) is injective, its differential is injective, and its inverse onto its image is continuous. It is therefore a smooth embedding. Its dimension is the dimension of \(\Theta_E\), namely \(p+\sum_j|\Pi^E_j|\), and its image is connected because \(\Theta_E=\mathbb R^{b_E}\times(0,\infty)^p\) is connected.

For relative closedness, for arbitrary \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) define the unrestricted parent-regression row
\[
 \widetilde B_{jP_j}(\Sigma)=\Sigma_{jP_j}\Sigma_{P_jP_j}^{-1},
 \qquad \widetilde B_{ji}(\Sigma)=0\quad(i\notin P_j).
\]
Then \(\Sigma\in\mathcal M(E)\) if and only if (i) \(\widetilde B_{ji}(\Sigma)=\widetilde B_{jk}(\Sigma)\) whenever \(i,k\) lie in the same block of \(\Pi^E_j\), and (ii)
\[
 (I_p-\widetilde B(\Sigma))\Sigma(I_p-\widetilde B(\Sigma))^{\mathsf T}
\]
is diagonal. Necessity follows from the recovered structural parameters above. Conversely, (i) assembles \(\widetilde B\) from a legal \(\beta_E\), while (ii) gives a diagonal innovation covariance; its diagonal is strictly positive because it is a congruence of \(\Sigma\) by the invertible acyclic matrix \(I_p-\widetilde B\). Hence the covariance formula in \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\) holds. Conditions (i)--(ii) are finitely many continuous rational equalities on the positive-definite cone, so their common zero set is relatively closed. Their only denominators are determinants of positive-definite principal submatrices, which are positive; multiplying them out gives equivalent polynomial equalities.

Finally evaluate the differential at \(\beta_E=0\) and \(\omega_E=(1,\ldots,1)\), which maps to \(I_p\). Differentiating the covariance formula yields
\[
 d\Sigma=dB_E+dB_E^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}(d\omega_E).
\]
The derivative in the coordinate \(\beta_{jB}\) is one precisely on the unordered off-diagonal coordinates \(\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}\), and the variance derivatives are diagonal. Projection off the diagonal gives the displayed tangent space. This also directly verifies the construction in \(\texttt{def:offdiagonal-tangent}\).

added_lemmas.statement: For blocked states \(C=(G,\Pi)\) and \(D=(H,\Lambda)\), equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies that \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent; in particular, they have the same skeleton and the same unshielded colliders.

source.verbatim_statement: Let \((G,c)\) and \((H,d)\) be model equivalent colored DAGs. Suppose that \(c\) is a vertex- (edge-) coloring and that \(d\) is a vertex- (edge-) coloring. Then \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent DAGs. Hence, they have the same skeleton and v-structures.

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2404.04024v3, Corollary 5.6 in the HTML version dated August 24, 2026.

added_lemmas.statement: Two directed acyclic graphs on the same labelled vertex set are Markov equivalent if and only if they have the same skeleton and the same unshielded colliders.

source.verbatim_statement: Two dags are equivalent if and only if they have the same skeletons and the same v-structures.

upstream.citation: Thomas Verma and Judea Pearl. Equivalence and Synthesis of Causal Models. Proceedings of the Sixth Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 220--227, 1990.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published-source scan at arXiv:1302.4938, page 88, where Chickering attributes the theorem to Verma and Pearl.

added_lemmas.statement: If the directed acyclic graphs \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent and \(\delta(C,D)\) of their common-skeleton edges have opposite orientations, then \(G\) can be transformed into \(H\) by exactly \(\delta(C,D)\) distinct covered-edge reversals. Every intermediate graph is acyclic and Markov equivalent to \(G\).

source.verbatim_statement: Let \(g\) and \(g'\) be any pair of dags such that \(g\) and \(g'\) are equivalent. There exists a sequence of \(|\Delta(g,g')|\) distinct edge reversals in \(g\) with the following properties: each edge reversed in \(g\) is a covered edge; after each reversal, \(g\) is a dag equivalent to \(g'\); and after all reversals, \(g=g'\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published-source scan at arXiv:1302.4938, Theorem 2, page 89; mathematical glyphs were normalized to LaTeX.

added_lemmas.statement: If \(E' = \operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}(E)\) is defined by \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\), then \(E'\in\mathfrak S_p\), the reverse transformation \(\operatorname{rev}_{j\to i}(E')\) is defined and equals \(E\), and \(\mathcal M(E')=\mathcal M(E)\). The nonsingleton families are preserved at every vertex.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(S=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(i)\). Definedness of the move gives
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)=S\cup\{i\},\qquad
 \{i\}\in\Pi^E_j,\qquad
 \Pi^E_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^E_i.
\]
Reversing a covered edge preserves acyclicity: if reversal of \(i\to j\) created a directed cycle, the old graph would contain a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\) other than the edge. If \(k\to j\) is the last edge of a shortest such path, coveredness gives \(k\to i\), which together with the initial segment \(i\leadsto k\) is already a directed cycle in \(G_E\), a contradiction. The transported partitions in \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\) partition the new parent sets, so \(E'\in\mathfrak S_p\). They also show directly that the reverse move is defined and returns \(E\).

It remains to prove equality of covariance images, rather than merely ordinary Markov equivalence. Conditional on \(X_S\), write the two affected structural equations as
\[
 X_i=a^{\mathsf T}X_S+\varepsilon_i,\qquad
 X_j=bX_i+d^{\mathsf T}X_S+\varepsilon_j,
\]
where \(u=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)>0\), \(v=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_j)>0\), and all innovations are mutually independent. Both \(a\) and \(d\) are constant on every block of the common partition \(\Pi^E_i\). Set
\[
 t=v+b^2u>0,\qquad q=\frac{bu}{t},\qquad
 \eta_j=b\varepsilon_i+\varepsilon_j,\qquad
 \eta_i=\varepsilon_i-q\eta_j.
\]
Direct substitution gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 X_j&=(d+ba)^{\mathsf T}X_S+\eta_j,\\
 X_i&=qX_j+\{a-q(d+ba)\}^{\mathsf T}X_S+\eta_i.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\eta_j)=t,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\eta_i)=\frac{uv}{t}>0,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_i,\eta_j)=bu-qt=0.
\]
The pair \((\eta_i,\eta_j)\) is jointly Gaussian, so zero covariance implies independence; being a linear transformation of \((\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j)\), it is also independent of every other innovation. Both new coefficient vectors \(d+ba\) and \(a-q(d+ba)\) remain constant on every common block, while the reversed coefficient \(q\) occupies the transported singleton \(\{j\}\). Thus every covariance in \(\mathcal M(E)\) lies in \(\mathcal M(E')\). Applying the same construction to the inverse legal move gives the reverse inclusion.

Finally, \(\Pi^{E'}_j=\Pi^E_i\) and \(\Pi^{E'}_i=\Pi^E_i\cup\{\{j\}\}\); hence their nonsingleton subfamilies equal the common nonsingleton family of \(i\) and \(j\), and all other partitions are unchanged. Therefore every \(\mathcal N_k\) is preserved.

added_lemmas.statement: Within the BPEC class of properly blocked edge-coloured directed acyclic graphs, equality of covariance models identifies the entire edge-coloured directed acyclic graph.

source.verbatim_statement: Let \([G,c]\) be the model equivalence class of a BPEC-DAG \((G,c)\). Then \(|\mathcal{BP}\cap[G,c]|=1\); i.e., an edge-colored DAG is structurally identifiable in the set of BPEC-DAGs.

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2404.04024v3, Theorem 5.17 in the HTML version dated August 24, 2026.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(p\) and let \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) be independent \(N_p(0,\Sigma_0)\) vectors with \(\Sigma_0\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\). If \(n\geq p\), then \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) almost surely. Let \(\operatorname{vech}\) stack the upper-triangular entries of a symmetric matrix, and let \(V_0\) be indexed by unordered pairs with entries \((V_0)_{ij,kl}=\Sigma_{0,ik}\Sigma_{0,jl}+\Sigma_{0,il}\Sigma_{0,jk}\). Then \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\) in \(L^2\), and
\[
 \sqrt n\,\operatorname{vech}(S_n-\Sigma_0)\ \Longrightarrow\ N(0,V_0),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(X_iX_j,X_kX_l)=(V_0)_{ij,kl}.
\]
The covariance \(V_0\) is positive definite on nonzero symmetric directions. Consequently every continuously differentiable scalar functional with nonzero derivative at \(\Sigma_0\) obeys the corresponding studentized plug-in delta limit.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(Z\) be the \(p\)-by-\(n\) matrix with columns \(\Sigma_0^{-1/2}X^{(r)}\). Its entries have a joint density. When \(n\geq p\), the set on which every \(p\)-by-\(p\) minor vanishes is the zero set of nonzero polynomials and has Lebesgue measure zero. Thus \(Z\), and hence the data matrix, has row rank \(p\) almost surely. Therefore \(S_n=n^{-1}XX^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite almost surely.

Differentiating the Gaussian moment-generating function \(\exp(t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_0t/2)\) four times at zero gives
\[
 \mathbb E[X_iX_jX_kX_l]
 =\Sigma_{0,ij}\Sigma_{0,kl}+\Sigma_{0,ik}\Sigma_{0,jl}+\Sigma_{0,il}\Sigma_{0,jk}.
\]
It follows that the displayed covariance formula holds and that
\(\mathbb E\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F^2=O(n^{-1})\), proving \(L^2\) convergence.

For the limit law, put \(W_r=\operatorname{vech}(X^{(r)}X^{(r)\mathsf T}-\Sigma_0)\). These vectors are independent, centered, have covariance \(V_0\), and have finite third moments. For each fixed vector \(t\), Taylor's formula for the characteristic function, with the cubic remainder bounded by the finite third moment, gives
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{i t^{\mathsf T}W_1/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}V_0t}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Taking the \(n\)-th power yields \(\exp(-t^{\mathsf T}V_0t/2)\), the characteristic function of \(N(0,V_0)\), which proves the stated convergence.

If \(A\neq0\) is symmetric, then the corresponding quadratic-form direction has variance
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(X^{\mathsf T}AX)=2\operatorname{tr}\{(\Sigma_0^{1/2}A\Sigma_0^{1/2})^2\}>0.
\]
Thus \(V_0\) is positive definite on symmetric coordinates. If \(f\) is continuously differentiable at \(\Sigma_0\), Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{f(S_n)-f(\Sigma_0)\}
 =\mathrm Df(\Sigma_0)[\sqrt n(S_n-\Sigma_0)]+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
The preceding characteristic-function limit gives the normal law. Replacing \(\Sigma_0\) in the polynomial covariance formula by \(S_n\) is consistent by \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\), so division by the plug-in standard error gives a standard normal limit whenever \(\mathrm Df(\Sigma_0)\neq0\).

proposed.statement: For any \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\), equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies equality of their skeletons and \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\in V\). More precisely, the inclusion-minimal nonempty supports in \(T_C^{\circ}\) are exactly \(\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}\) for \(B\in\Pi_j\); every support of size at least two has a unique center \(j\) and recovers the labelled block \(B\), while a support of size one recovers only the underlying edge. Thus every edge whose orientation differs between \(G\) and \(H\) is a singleton block in both states.
proposed.justification: The tangent support partition is the first orientation-robust observable that distinguishes repeated incoming coefficient blocks from reversible singleton edges.
proposed.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 4.1 and Section 5, gives smoothness and fixed-graph rational recovery but no cross-DAG recovery of target-local blocks from equality of model images.
proposed.consumer: The lemma lets a covariance-model comparison recover causal communities without knowing which Markov-equivalent orientation generated them.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses the explicit smooth-embedding and tangent calculation supplied by the new geometry lemma.

proposed.statement: Let \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\) satisfy \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), and suppose \(x\to y\) is in \(G\) while \(y\to x\) is in \(H\). Then \(\mathcal N_x(C)=\mathcal N_y(C)\). Specifically, if \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) is split across two blocks of \(\Pi_y\), choosing unit innovation variances, coefficient one on \(x\to y\), coefficient one on a block \(T\in\Pi_y\) meeting but not containing \(S\), and zero elsewhere gives a covariance in \(\mathcal M(C)\) whose regression of \(X_x\) on \(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\) has coefficient \(-q\mathbf 1\{s\in T\}\) on \(s\in S\), with \(q=(2+|T\setminus(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\setminus\{y\})|)^{-1}>0\), contradicting the block \(S\) in \(D\).
proposed.justification: This sparse covariance witness is the load-bearing necessity step because it handles arbitrary extra target parents and simultaneous arrow changes.
proposed.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Lemma 5.11 and the proof of Theorem 5.17, separates reversals only in the proper-colouring regime; it does not establish the endpoint-family condition when singleton blocks coexist with repeated blocks.
proposed.consumer: The separator certifies when a proposed singleton reversal changes the complete covariance model, preventing a learner from merging observationally distinguishable causal-community states.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The separator needs the cited ordinary Markov-equivalence consequence and the explicit regression recovery from the geometry lemma.

proposed.statement: For every \(C=(G,\Pi),D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathfrak S_p\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\); \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\), equivalently \(G,H\) have the same skeleton and unshielded colliders, \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for all \(j\in V\), and every edge joining vertices with unequal nonsingleton families has the same orientation; and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\). Every step in the final characterization is a partition-compatible singleton covered reversal with the prescribed transport. Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\), and a shortest path reverses each disagreeing arrow exactly once. When every block is nonsingleton, \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), recovering and strictly extending the BPEC structural-identifiability result of BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 to the singleton-allowing blocked class.
proposed.justification: The theorem supplies both an exact static recovery functional and a complete local transformation calculus for the largest target-blocked coefficient class that contains ordinary DAG equivalence.
proposed.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 5.17, excludes singleton edge-colour classes and Question 5.19 asks for graphical edge-coloured equivalence; Chickering1995, Theorem 2, transports ordinary DAGs but has no coefficient-partition legality condition.
proposed.consumer: An extension of the colouredDAGs workflow can report the exact covariance-equivalence component instead of one arbitrary blocked DAG while retaining all repeated-coefficient communities.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete proof spine includes the two classical graph results, the proved local covariance invariance, and the published BPEC boundary.

proposed.statement: For every \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\). Static equality can be decided using \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons with adjacency matrices and canonical block bitsets. The enumeration is duplicate-free by exact state memoization, terminates after at most \(p!\) emitted states, and a breadth-first predecessor tree returns for every emitted \(D\) a shortest path of length \(\delta(C,D)\).
proposed.justification: The population equivalence theorem becomes operational only after it yields a terminating complete enumerator and shortest certificates.
proposed.gap: WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 gives linear-delay enumeration for ordinary Markov classes with fixed background knowledge, but does not handle state-dependent partition transport; the present guaranteed algorithm is finite and output-bounded rather than linear-delay.
proposed.consumer: Component enumeration supplies every graph-specific adjustment and path functional needed for possible-effect analysis under blocked coefficient information.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The enumeration proof directly uses invertibility of every legal reversal in addition to the main characterization.

proposed.statement: If every block of \(C\) is a singleton, then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for all \(j\) and \(\mathcal R(C)\) is exactly the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\), with \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}=\delta\) as in Chickering1995. If no block of \(C\) is a singleton, then every edge is fixed and \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\) as in the BPEC identifiability boundary. If \(G=H\) and \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), then \(\Pi=\Lambda\).
proposed.justification: The two extreme partitions verify that the characterization interpolates exactly between ordinary Markov equivalence and proper blocked identifiability.
proposed.gap: The two endpoint results are published separately by Chickering1995 and BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026; their exact interpolation within one full-model criterion is new.
proposed.consumer: These reductions provide regression tests for software and prevent interpreting every fixed arrow as a numerically identified direct effect.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The reduction proof directly invokes the classical Markov criterion, tangent recovery, and the cited BPEC boundary.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(p\), \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), and a parameter \(\theta_C\in\Theta_C\setminus\mathcal E_C\) with \(\Sigma_0=\phi_C(\theta_C)\). For each integer \(n\geq p\), let \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) be independent \(N_p(0,\Sigma_0)\) observations and let \(\widehat C_n\) be the deterministically tie-broken global minimizer in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\). Then \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) almost surely. Consequently every statewise block Gram matrix \(\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)\) is invertible, every constrained residual variance in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\) is strictly positive, and only the finite attained likelihood branch is used. As \(n\to\infty\) through integers satisfying \(n\geq p\),
\[
 \Pr\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
The exceptional set is proper algebraic: models of dimension at most \(d_C\) are excluded by their nonzero pulled-back defining polynomials, while larger models lose by the diverging dimension penalty. This is component recovery, not consistency of greedy GECS.
proposed.justification: Singleton blocks change the estimable structural target from one state to an exact quotient component, so selection consistency must quotient identical covariance images.
proposed.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Section 6 and Discussion, derives a decomposable BIC and reports GECS simulations but leaves consistency open; Haughton1988 treats finitely many smooth models without the blocked-state equality quotient.
proposed.consumer: A fixed-dimensional coloured-DAG analysis can consistently report the right component even when several singleton-block orientations have exactly equal likelihood.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The direct fixed-dimensional BIC proof uses the proved blocked-model geometry and Gaussian sample-covariance calculus.

proposed.statement:
Under the conditions of \(\texttt{thm:generic-bic-component-recovery}\), fix finite \(\mathcal Q\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Along integers \(n\geq p\), the event \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) has probability one. Hence every \(L_E(S_n)\) is obtained from the uniquely solvable block-constrained Gram systems in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\), and every derivative \(\mathrm D g_E(S_n)\) is evaluated inside the positive-definite cone on which \(g_E\) is rational and smooth. Then \(\mathcal T_{\widehat C_n}(S_n)\) converges in probability to \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\) in Hausdorff distance. With \(\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\) defined memberwise before removing numerical duplicates,
\[
 \liminf_{\substack{n\to\infty\\ n\geq p}}\Pr\left\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\text{ and }g_E(\Sigma_0)\text{ belongs to its labelled interval in }\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\text{ for every }E\in\mathcal R(C)\right\}\geq1-\alpha.
\]
The conclusion permits coincident effect values and singular joint covariance because only marginal nonconstant-coordinate variances enter the Bonferroni construction.
proposed.justification: The observationally identified object is a finite set of possible effects, so valid inference must cover all component members rather than one selected graph.
proposed.gap: MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009 proves consistency of possible-effect multisets without simultaneous intervals, while ChangGuoMalinsky2026 targets coverage of one fixed true effect after graph screening rather than every member of a full-model-equivalence effect set.
proposed.consumer: An analyst using the Sachs protein network can report simultaneous uncertainty for every total effect compatible with the recovered coefficient-community component.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly uses the structural equivalence theorem and the fixed-dimensional Gaussian covariance and delta calculations.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Whether exact quotienting by equality of the rational maps \(g_E\) admits deterministic output-polynomial total time or polynomial delay while retaining a certificate for every state.
open_obligations.obstruction: Compact arithmetic-circuit equality for the rational effect maps reduces after denominator clearing to exact polynomial identity testing; deterministic polynomial-time canonicalization is not supplied by the frozen core. In addition, the number of states can be much larger than the number of distinct functionals, so ordinary breadth-first traversal does not give delay measured in distinct outputs.
open_obligations.attempted: The component was enumerated by legal-reversal breadth-first search, transported partitions were reconstructed from endpoint parent sets and invariant nonsingleton families, and exact rational functions were compared after clearing denominators. This closes correctness and path independence but not the requested complexity bound.
open_obligations.partial_result: There is a terminating exact procedure, but no output-polynomial or polynomial-delay bound is established. Breadth-first search enumerates every state in \(\mathcal R(C)\), stores the shortest predecessor certificate of length \(\delta(C,E)\), and computes each \(g_E\) as a rational arithmetic expression. The transported partition is path independent because the endpoint graph and the invariant families \((\mathcal N_j)_{j\in V}\) uniquely determine it. Equality of two resulting rational maps is decidable by cross-multiplying their positive Gram-determinant denominators and expanding the resulting polynomial identity, so exact equality classes and one representative per class can be returned after all states are visited. This proves finite exact duplicate removal with shortest certificates, but its running time is controlled by \(|\mathcal R(C)|\) and by expanded polynomial size, not by the number of distinct effect functionals.
